market.summary_html: The Maps leaderboard is reshuffling. Across the same 11-month window we've been tracking, the prior leaders are losing ground — Glam Shots down 283 top-3 cells, VIP Party Photo Booth down 381 — while three brands rose from near-zero: Captured Fun (+358), Luxe Booth (+319), Capture Pod (+274). That's a moment of category-flux. Brands with strong foundations who align their GBP correctly can move up the leaderboard fast — that's the exact opportunity the 90-day plan below targets.

meta.scope: Maps recovery diagnosis — GBP and on-page first. Eight tracked queries across 11 months of HQDM tenure (Aug 5 2025 → May 6 2026), plus competitive read.
meta.focus: A Maps-only diagnosis. We did not analyze GSC or GA4 in this pass — pull both before the next monthly review so the recovery curve has matching traffic + lead data attached.

tldr: The Maps gap is structural, not effort. MIA's Google Business profile primary category is Photography service; five of the eight top-3 dominators citywide run Photo booth as primary (Glam Shots wins 419 top-3 cells with only 15 reviews — the category match is doing the lifting). On top of that, the site footer phone is (786) 973-9973 — the GBP's chat/SMS number — while the GBP primary phone is (786) 833-7645; that NAP mismatch suppresses the trust signal Google uses to associate the site with the profile. Fix those two and the foundation (124 backlinks, 103 reviews, 739-cell average reach) is positioned to convert.

headline.h2: Root cause is two GBP-level fixes — not site depth
headline.lede: Across 11 months of LD scans (Aug 5 2025 → May 6 2026), MIA's average rank sits at 10.69 on the latest scan (weighted across 8 tracked queries) with 43 top-3 cells out of 663 cells reached. The two highest-intent terms — "wedding photo booth rental" and "360 photo booth rental" — show zero top-3 cells in the latest scan. Meanwhile competitors with materially weaker review profiles (Glam Shots: 15 reviews; Luxe Booth: 11; Captured Fun: 35) all sit at 300+ top-3 cells citywide. The distinguishing feature is the GBP primary category.

gbp_audit.intro: Twelve elements scored against the eight top-3 Maps dominators in the same market. The two red rows below are the unlock — every other element on the profile is already healthy.

rows.should_be: Photo booth — used as primary by 5 of the 8 top-3 dominators (Glam Shots, 360 Photo Booth Miami Rental, Miami Event Photo Booth, Capture Pod, The Photobomb Booths). Google's category model rewards a literal match to the user query; "photo booth rental" maps to Photo booth, not Photography service.
rows.evidence: Glam Shots Miami (15 reviews, 5.0★) outranks MIA (103 reviews, 5.0★) in 419 grid cells vs MIA's latest 43 — the variable that explains the gap is category, not reviews.

rows.current: Photo lab · Photography shop · Photo agency · Photographer · Photography studio · Party equipment rental service
rows.should_be: Replace the stacked photography-only secondaries with: Photo booth (if not used as primary), Wedding photographer, Event planner, Party planner. Photo lab and Photography shop hurt category clarity — they pull the listing toward film-developing intent.
rows.evidence: VIP Party Photo Booth (316 reviews, Party equipment rental service primary) still holds 310 top-3 cells — the right vertical stack beats reviews-as-volume.

rows.current: MIA Photo Booth - No.1 Photo Booth Rental
rows.should_be: Keep. Includes the head term twice. The descriptor "No.1 Photo Booth Rental" walks the GBP-naming line but isn't a violation under current guidelines.

rows.current: 210-word description, includes 360 / Glam / Black-and-White / Roamer keywords + Miami + weddings/corporate/private parties. Open since 2020.
rows.should_be: Keep. Small upgrade: add "photo booth rental" twice (currently once); add the secondary-target phrase "wedding photo booth" explicitly.

rows.current: Roamer · Black and White · Glam · Social · Studio · 360 · plus umbrella "Photo Booth Rental in Miami"
rows.should_be: Keep all seven. Add a wedding-specific service ("Wedding Photo Booth in Miami") and corporate-specific ("Corporate Event Photo Booth in Miami") so the services list cleanly addresses the two highest-intent query buckets.

rows.current: Women-owned · Latino-owned · LGBTQ+ friendly · English · Spanish
rows.should_be: Keep all five. Add "Online appointments" and "Online estimates" attributes if available — both surface in the local pack UI for service-area businesses.

rows.current: 20 cities declared — Doral, Miami, Hialeah, Kendall, Opa-locka, Miami Beach, etc.
rows.should_be: Keep — broad service-area declarations don't suppress Maps for service-area businesses. But: the website should mirror the same cities in dedicated, indexable pages with consistent NAP. Today's site lists 27 area pages — overlap is partial, slugs are random.
rows.evidence: Site URLs use a different city set (Town Park Estates, Granada, Spring Garden, Gladeview, Coral Groves) than the GBP service area — the two layers don't reinforce each other.

connection.intro: Five elements of the website↔GBP handshake. The site is built — 27 area pages, 6 service pages, 60 blog posts — but the bones aren't connected. The most consequential break is the phone number; the rest compound it.
connection.verdict: The website doesn't currently reinforce the GBP. Until the phone number, schema and URL structure match, every link Google follows from the GBP into the site reads as a weak association.

rows.detail: The GBP primary phone is (786) 833-7645. The site footer and every service/area page show (786) 973-9973 — which is actually the GBP's chat/SMS number.
rows.fix: Global replace across the theme: swap (786) 973-9973 for (786) 833-7645 in header, footer, schema, contact form, structured-data tel: links. Keep the SMS number only on a dedicated "Text us" button (sms: protocol).

rows.detail: The homepage and area pages return no JSON-LD LocalBusiness or Service schema. The richest signal MIA could send Google is currently missing entirely.
rows.fix: Add LocalBusiness schema sitewide (theme head), with sameAs pointing to the Google Maps CID URL + the 6 social profiles already in the GBP. Add Service schema on the 6 service pages. FAQPage schema on /frequently-asked-questions.

rows.issue: URL structure — 27 location pages with random adjective slugs
rows.detail: The 27 area pages use a different adjective per slug: /leading-photo-booth-rental-in-coral-gables-fl, /famous-..., /premier-..., etc. This is the fingerprint of programmatic-template content.
rows.fix: Consolidate to a clean /photo-booth-rental/[city]/ structure with 301 redirects from the old slugs.

rows.detail: Today the site has a service axis (6 booth-type pages) and a location axis (27 area pages) but no cell-level pages combining the two.
rows.fix: Build a 6×15 matrix (6 services × 15 highest-priority cities = 90 pages) over 90 days. Each page ~400 words of unique copy.

rows.issue: Internal linking — area pages don't link to service pages
rows.detail: Sampled three area pages (Coral Gables, Wynwood, Midtown Miami): each links only to homepage and sibling area pages.
rows.fix: Add a 3-paragraph "Booth types we bring to [city]" block to every area page with inline links to each of the 6 service pages. Reverse block on each service page ("Most-requested neighborhoods").

levers.title: Internal linking + GBP posts cadence
levers.summary: Add a "Booth types in [city]" block to every area page (6 inbound links each); reverse block on each service page. Restart weekly GBP posts.

owner_asks.q: Top 5 revenue cities — can you confirm?
owner_asks.why: We're proposing the new /photo-booth-rental/[city]/ structure for 15 priority cities. We'd like the team's read on the 5 cities that drive the most actual bookings — so the first content sprint hits revenue-weighted, not just GBP-area-weighted.

owner_asks.q: Internal phone-routing on (786) 833-7645 — confirmed live and answered?
owner_asks.why: Before we push the global phone swap on the site and citations, we want to make sure the GBP primary number routes to a human and tracks the way the chat number does today.

owner_asks.q: Capacity for the 90-page matrix build — internal copywriter or HQDM?
owner_asks.why: We can write the 90 cells in-house or hand a template + city list to an internal writer. Confirming the path so we can sequence Month 1-3 accurately.

owner_asks.q: GA4 + GSC access — can we get added?
owner_asks.why: miaphotobooth.net is not yet in our authorized GSC properties. With both connected we can put a real organic-clicks-and-leads recovery curve next to the Maps recovery, the same way we do for AQMS and Maison.

The LD scans show MIA dropped from 67 top-3 cells in Aug to 2 in Sept, then recovered to 74 in Oct. Worth knowing if there was a GBP issue, category swap, or temporary suspension we should factor into the recovery model.
